title: Influence of individual models and studies on quantitative mitigation findings in the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report
crossref_metadata.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

records.canonical_title: Influence of individual models and studies on quantitative mitigation findings in the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report
records.assessment_method: AI-assisted comparison of publisher metadata, Crossref metadata and the source passages listed under locator.
records.metadata_notes: Publisher and Crossref title, author order, bibliographic year and pagination or article number agree. Full author list retained. Publisher and Crossref both spell the first surname Sognnaes.
records.claim_supported: The study tests 27 AR6 WGIII Summary for Policymakers mitigation findings by removing individual models and studies from the scenarios database. Several reported medians change substantially, and the effects depend on both representation and scenario positioning. Model- or study-weighting does not remove dependence on sample composition.
locator: Results, "Influence of individual models and studies on key AR6 mitigation findings": 27 findings, leave-one-model/study-out calculations and changes in median outcomes.
Results, "Median values depend on the choice of weighting and sampling": alternative weights.
Fig. 4 and accompanying text: representation and positioning relative to the median.
records.claim_fit: Demonstrates that numerical representation and influence on assessment findings are distinct quantities. Its scenario-grain analysis does not establish which bibliographic records caused changes in assessment conclusions.
records.source_scope: Publisher abstract, Introduction and relevant full-text Results sections and figure captions read.
